references.text: The Lord showed Moses the same sign at the burning bush, where the staff turned into a snake as a sign of God's power.
God's command to Moses and Aaron to throw the staff before Pharaoh, which verse 10 fulfills.
Egypt's magicians imitate the sign with their own staffs, but Aaron's staff swallows theirs.
Moses was commanded to take the staff to perform signs with it, something now carried out through Aaron.
Reference to treading on snakes and dragons (tannin), showing God's power over such creatures.
Pharaoh is compared to a great sea monster (tannin), the same Hebrew word used for the snake in Exodus 7:10.
Paul mentions Jannes and Jambres as those who opposed Moses, a tradition linked to the magicians who imitated this sign.
Both are part of the same series of miracles where the staff is used as an instrument of God's judgment against Egypt.
Verse 4:3 is the private confirmation of the sign that in 7:10 becomes public judgment against Pharaoh.
Contrast between the snake as a sign of God's power against Pharaoh and the snake as an instrument of judgment over Israel's sin.
